name: Example: Computing Iterations of the Newton-Raphson Method Using Linear Systems
problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,1]\times[0,1] \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2,$ where

$$
f(x,y) = xy^2+3x^2-xy-x.
$$

Find the matrix equation that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $\big[ 1, \: 1 \big]^T,$ and compute the components of the first iteration
worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ is

$$
\mathbf{x}_{n+1} = \mathbf{x}_n - [H_f(\mathbf{x}_n)]^{-1} \nabla{f}(\mathbf{x}_n),
$$

where $H(\mathbf{x}_n)$ and $\nabla{f}(\mathbf{x}_n)$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at $\mathbf{x}_n.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be rewritten as

$$
H_f(\mathbf{x}_n)(\mathbf{x}_{n+1} - \mathbf{x}_n) = -\nabla{f}(\mathbf{x}_n).
$$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2}+3{x}^{2}-xy-x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{2}+3{x}^{2}-xy-x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+6x-y-1 \\ 2xy-x\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}+6x-y-1) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy-x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}+6x-y-1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy-x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 2y-1 \\ 2y-1 & 2x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14074707/assets/ddb94c6d067c419b06cdbec87426e70db6ee07acca7d42c0900ae386f6fe37ae.png)

Starting with ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14074707/assets/8bdb55b26b462507d9810675499558be66e7b970d2f9fdb78e708807e617ce8d.png) we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}6 & 2y-1 \\ 2y-1 & 2x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+6x-y-1 \\ 2xy-x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & 2(1)-1 \\ 2(1)-1 & 2(1)\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}(1)^{2}+6(1)-(1)-1 \\ 2(1)(1)-1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system of equations, we get ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14074707/assets/daee26a8f82011d916bf04d7e374a2b8f471602877fe76335f7f1b242ca86b00.png) Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}+[\begin{aligned}-9/11 \\ -1/11\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-9/11 \\ -1/11\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}0.182 \\ 0.909\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
